articles.title: We Sat Down with D&D Game Designer James Wyatt to Talk Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft
articles.summary: At New York Comic Con, I got a chance to sit down with Wizards of the Coast Principal Game Designer James Wyatt to talk about the first Universes Beyond expansion for D&D.
body: Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft is less than a month away, and it already looks like it's going to be a massive expansion to the tabletop game. But there are still a lot of questions about whether this new expansion is going to lean more towards the combat-oriented approach of the MMO or just be a traditional D&D game on Azeroth.

IGN: I know that there are a lot of people who play both WoW and D&D, and I've heard some WoW players say that this is going to get them into D&D. Does the Expansion have a good on-ramp for those players?

articles.title: 7 Crazy Movie Premises That Actually Worked
articles.summary: Before Whalefall, these crazy movie premises actually worked too.
body: “A young man is swallowed by a whale while searching for his father’s remains deep in the ocean.”

That is the elevator pitch for Whalefall, starring Austin Abrams (Resident Evil) and co-written by Daniel Kraus and director Brian Duffield (No One Will Save You). Set for release on October 16, the film is based on Kraus’ 2023 novel, inspired by a viral video of kayakers seemingly being swallowed by a whale. Whalefall’s central conceit is one writers and directors are challenged by, and often dream of, because it raises the questions: Can I pull this off? And how can I make this work? In other words, the absolutely bonkers premise is fertile ground for real creative risk and opportunity.
points: Before Whalefall, these crazy movie premises actually worked too.

articles.title: 2026 Has Been a Surprisingly Excellent Year for Shooters
articles.summary: All the way back in January, it seemed like 2026 might be a rough year for fans of shooters. Highguard ’s launch and almost immediate delaunch created an anxiety around the genre that was hard to shake.
body: Rumors of the shooter’s demise were greatly exaggerated, it turns out. Looking back at the year from October’s vantage point, 2026 has turned out to be a landmark year for the genre. While sales have been erratic at times, this year has given us plenty of big-budget and indie shooters alike that have revitalized a category that needed some fresh blood.

Xbox has been a major player in that charge, despite having a disastrous year from a business perspective. Even so, the studios working under the publisher have still found a way to deliver a handful of hits. Chief among them is Gear of War: E-Day, which has been a hit with critics and players alike since launch. It’s a highly polished throwback to the golden age of cover-based shooters, one that packs a lot of delicious brutality into a lore-expanding prequel campaign. With Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 positioned as a similar return to glory, Xbox could wind up with two behemoths on its hands this year.

articles.title: Whalefall Isn't Really About a Whale, Says Josh Brolin
articles.summary: While at New York Comic Con 2026, a week before the film’s release, Polygon caught up with stars Josh Brolin and Austin Abrams, as well as Kraus and Duffield, to talk about the biggest challenges of bringing this book to the big screen, as well as what the movie is really about.
body: Whalefall is now in theaters. Based on the novel by Daniel Kraus ( Angel Down ), who also co-wrote the screenplay with director Brian Duffield ( No One Will Save You, Cocaine Bear ), Whalefall is about a scuba diver (Austin Abrams) looking for the remains of his father ( Josh Brolin ) in the Pacific Ocean. However, while he’s on his expedition, he gets swallowed by an enormous sperm whale. With only an hour’s worth of oxygen, he must free himself from inside the whale.

According to Kraus, the toughest part of the inside-the-whale experience was bringing to life the stomach of the whale — or, more accurately, the first stomach, as sperm whale stomachs consist of four separate chambers.
Austin Abrams, who stars in Whalefall as diver Jay Gardiner, pointed to the same scene as the most difficult, saying the hardest part of the film was “the compression, being squeezed.”
As much as the movie is about a guy getting swallowed by a whale, neither Kraus nor Duffield ever saw the whale as the film’s villain.

articles.title: The Street Fighter Movie Makes a Mistake Mortal Kombat Already Learned From
articles.summary: Why are fighting game movies so scared of fighting tournaments? The Street Fighter movie is just the latest example.
body: Put on your gis and gloves, fighting fans, because Street Fighter is now in theaters. The latest attempt to adapt the venerated fighting game franchise for the big screen may not be getting off to the best start with critics, but fans of the series will likely go check it out for themselves. The film does have its positive aspects, such as the gorgeous 2D animation used for flashback sequences as well as plenty of easter eggs and fighting moves ripped right from the classic games. But as a whole, Street Fighter is too slapdash to be a fully satisfying cinematic experience, and one of the biggest reasons why is that the film doesn’t use the seemingly obvious way to structure itself.

articles.title: The Best Transformers Movie That No One Watched Finds New Life on Streaming
articles.summary: Under director Michael Bay, Paramount built a billion-dollar franchise across five live-action Transformers movies. But after Bay's final turn behind the camera, 2017's Transformers: The Last Knight, the robots-in-disguise franchise started to go in unpredictable new directions.
body: Paramount swerved in 2024 with one of the best Transformers movies to date, the animated prequel Transformers One. While it didn't light up the box office or please every Transformers fan, the origin story of Optimus Prime and Megatron is finding a new life on streaming.

Transformers One was recently added to Netflix after a multiyear run on Paramount Plus. Netflix audiences are giving the animated feature another shot, according to streaming data from FlixPatrol. Transformers One quickly landed in the top 10 most-watched movies on Netflix this week, charting at No. 6 in the U.S. It's nestled between Twilight — it's officially "Hoa hoa hoa" season — and the animated comedy Ice Age.

Netflix viewers are right to give Transformers One the overdue attention it deserves. As we said in our review of the film, it's "sweet, occasionally heartbreaking, and utterly convincing in telling an origin story for friends-turned-foes Optimus Prime and Megatron. Thanks to its strong cast and a solid story buttressed by a classic hero’s journey, Transformers One has a spark that we’ve rarely seen in a Transformers flick..."

articles.title: Early Modern Warfare 4 Consensus Unanimous That It Features On Of The Best COD Campaigns Ever
articles.summary: The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign released on Oct. 16 for those who pre-ordered the game digitally, so first reactions to it are finally rolling in. So far, sentiment around this part of the new Call of Duty is positive, with many fans praising the campaign.
body: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's campaign takes the action to South Korea, as Price fights against Makarov and a new threat called The Archer reaches new heights just as a war between North and South Korea breaks out. It's a high-stakes political and military thriller, and has some open-ended levels that tease out the impending DMZ mode. While Black Ops 7's campaign was one of the most derided aspects of last year's Call of Duty, the opposite is the case for Modern Warfare 4.

A quick look at the top posts on the Modern Warfare 4 subreddit shows how much players are loving the campaign. User Havkas called it the "best campaign since original trilogy," elaborating that it "plays like a perfect blend of the modern entries and the original trilogy." This sentiment is felt across the subreddit, as fans see the campaign as a return to form for the Modern Warfare franchise after some relatively weaker recent campaigns. In one comment, user Resting-Tiger goes as far as to say the game has " MW2 OG levels of storytelling," favorably comparing it to one of the best Call of Duty campaigns ever.

articles.title: Gameplay footage emerges of reportedly cancelled Assassin's Creed game Destiny
articles.summary: Footage of a reportedly cancelled Assassin's Creed game set in ancient China has emerged online, including stealth kills, the series' leap of faith, and a spinning umbrella weapon.
body: Called Assassin's Creed Destiny, it was reportedly being made for current platforms at Tencent -owned TiMi Studio Group, which also worked on mobile game Assassin's Creed Jade.

According to MP1st, the clips were taken from portfolios belonging to people who worked on it, and most come from a prototype built in February 2025. It's thought Destiny's setting was 206 BCE, nine years after Jade's 215 BCE.

The main mission has a female assassin heading into a sacred palace under siege from the army of the warlord Xiang Yu, in search of a mysterious artefact, and an early-stage boss encounter involving the warlord also appears.

Elsewhere, a male character uses parkour to dispatch enemies, while a temporary test area shows the player using an umbrella-style spinning weapon, with ink-brush ability icons and a health bar on screen.

articles.summary: I've nothing against games that feature simulated animal petting, but it's never been something I've considered buying a game specifically for. Sure, it's nice when your character can stroke a virtual dog or fuss with a clump of polygons shaped like a cat, but it rarely amounts to more than a…
body: The Blood of Dawnwalker already features a directional combat system in the vein of Kingdom Come: Deliverance. And this system lies at the heart of the animal petting being added to version 1.1 of the vampire RPG—according to an update the developer posted on X: "What happens when you merge a directional combat system with an ability to pet dogs and cats?" Rebel Wolves asked. "Directional. Animal. Petting."

Sadly, Rebel Wolves didn't provide any further detail about this system. But it did offer plenty of insight into what else is coming with update 1.1. Aside from being able to stroke cats at different angles, perhaps the most significant addition is a new Story mode. This will feature an "additional combat assist" for players who aren't interested in mastering the game's swordplay, letting them focus mainly on enjoying the narrative and making decisions. articles.title: Steam's Achievement Sets beta aims to stop new content breaking your completion status
articles.summary: Valve is beta testing Steam Achievement Sets, a feature that lets developers group a game's achievements into collections.
body: In an announcement, the company said that games "live longer than ever, continuing to receive updates through new DLC, expansions, and seasons", but that achievements added with new content "can be hard to discover and can accidentally break the completion status of players who have already finished the game".

That's why developers can now specify the number of sets and the purpose of each "to match their game's specific needs", so one game might group its achievements into single-player and multiplayer groups, while another could use eight class-based sets. Players still unlock achievements as usual, and Steam then sorts what they've unlocked into the developer-created sets, which Valve says makes it "easier to see what you have completed and to find other related achievements you can unlock next".
Each set has its own progress bar, and completing one adds a "set complete" trophy to the player's profile. If new achievements are later added to a set, completion is "preserved".
points: Valve is beta testing Steam Achievement Sets, a feature that lets developers group a game's achievements into collections.

articles.title: Art of Rally follow-up Over the Hill's biggest success is finding a way to be a driving game that asks you to take it slow
articles.summary: I'd nearly forgotten Over the Hill's predecessor, Art of Rally, was a racing game. But that's not meant as a slight. It's just that, for all the happy hours I poured into it, I don't recall doing a single race.
body: Over the Hill very much feels like Art of Rally's free-roam mode writ large. Here the entire focus is on unhurried off-road exploration across large open swathes of stylised, vividly hued wilderness. And the vibe of its minimalist roaming, its uninsistent structure, very definitely skews toward 'chill'. Which is to say, if you're the kind of person who craves direction and explicit goals, or who's looking for speedy racing thrills, I don't think this is the adventure for you. But if, like me, you count yourself among the sandbox explorers, the curious meanderers, the tranquility seekers of the world, it offers its own special kind of driving thrill.

articles.title: Developer cancels public demo of its upcoming horror drinking game, fearing it will be instantly cloned by AI vibe coders: 'We sincerely apologise for the short notice'
articles.summary: The developer of an upcoming horror drinking game has cancelled plans for a public Steam demo in favour of private preview sessions, citing concerns that AI vibe coders might use the demo's content to clone the game.
body: Drunken Goddess Reflux is a "shot glass Russian roulette" drinking game where players square off against an anime demon girl who loves you but also kind of wants to murder you (which sounds like a standard relationship to me), with the goal of getting your girl-frenemy so blotto that she barfs up her soul. Frankly, it doesn't sound like my cup of tequila, although there is a mechanic where the rules of the game grow weirder and wilder the more alcohol you imbibe—which sounds neat.

Regardless, developer Alliance Arts planned to release a Steam demo on October 19, but in a post on X (via Rock, Paper, Shotgun ), the studio explained this is no longer the case. Instead, the studio will host "closed online play sessions for a limited number of participants."

"We sincerely apologize for the short notice," Alliance Arts added, before explaining its reasoning behind the demo's cancellation. Apparently, the demo would have come with "some restrictions on posting and streaming gameplay videos", which Alliance Arts decided it wouldn't be able to properly manage.

articles.title: Funcom is laying off yet more developers as it pivots to supporting Dune: Awakening and Conan Exiles
articles.summary: Funcom, the developer behind Dune: Awakening and Conan Exiles, has announced a restructuring process that will result in layoffs at the company, and that current CEO Rui Casais will leave Funcom once the reorganisation is complete.
body: The decision comes after a shift in direction at Funcom, whereby the studio will focus wholly on supporting its existing survival RPGs. In a statement (via GamesIndustry.biz ) Casais said that Dune: Awakening was "the biggest project we have ever undertaken, requiring many years of significant development resources across our studios". He continued that "moving from full production into long-term post-launch development and operations requires a different organisation.

"While we would have wanted everyone who helped build Dune: Awakening to continue with us, we cannot sustain the size and structure required during peak development as we move into this next phase. My focus now is ensuring the process is as supportive as possible for everyone affected, and to treat our colleagues with the respect and transparency they deserve."

Dune: Awakening was a big hit for Funcom when it was released in June last year, with the survival MMO shifting a million copies in two weeks to become the fastest-selling game in the Norwegian developer's history. Despite this initial success, however, the longer-term performance of the game is harder to gauge.

articles.title: Red Rising Greenlit for Movie Adaptation With Author Pierce Brown to Produce
articles.summary: The Red Rising book series by author Pierce Brown has officially been greenlit for a movie adaptation from Paramount Pictures, with Hunger Games alum Francis Lawrence to direct. Red Rising is getting the Hollywood treatment more than a decade after it was first published in 2014.
body: Lawrence is known for his work on another young adult screen adaptation in the Hunger Games series, having directed every movie in the franchise sans the first one, which was directed by Gary Ross. Lawrence recently directed Stephen King adaptation The Long Walk, as well as the forthcoming Sunrise on the Reaping, the latest movie in the Hunger Games franchise.

Lawrence is also set to produce the Red Rising film alongside Cameron MacConomy for their about:blank production company, as well as Francesco Goedhuis and the author of the Red Rising saga himself, Pierce Brown.
Brown reacted to the news in a post on his Instagram account, writing, "Let fall the iron rain. Bloodydamn, I love this team."

Joining Red Rising is Justin Rhodes, who will write the movie’s script. Eagle-eyed IGN readers will recognize this name, as he is also involved in Netflix’s live-action Bioshock movie, which is reportedly still in early development. Rhodes is known for films like Terminator: Dark Fate, Traveler, and Liminal.

videos.summary: STRANGER THAN HEAVEN is a fifty-year, action-adventure saga of men with nowhere to go and their desperate struggle to find a home. Use extreme violence to survive, and musical talent to thrive as a showman across five cities and eras of modern Japan. Coming to PlayStation 5 on January 15, 2027.
body: In this trailer, discover the events that lead Makoto Daito to sneak aboard the ship of a man named Orpheus, and the harsh realities and life-changing encounters that await him once arriving in the city of Kokura, Japan.
Additional trailers spotlighting Daito's life in each of the five cities and eras featured throughout the game will be released in the future. Stay tuned for more.
